Be specific: "We were working on listing the latest 5 properties from jv_deals. I showed you ONE STOP CONSTRUCTORS, PEREZ RESIDENCE, and Casa Rosario. Want me to pull that again?"

   170|export function buildCompactContextPrefix(liveContextBlock?: string): string {
   171|  if (!liveContextBlock) return '';
   172|
   173|  const shaMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Commit SHA:\s*(\S+)/);
   174|  const fullShaMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Full SHA:\s*(\S+)/);
   175|  const statusMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Status:\s*(\S+)/);
   176|  const bootMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Boot Time:\s*(.+)/);
   177|  const envMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Environment:\s*(\S+)/);
   178|  const schedulerMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Running:\s*(\S+)/);
   179|  const timestampMatch = liveContextBlock.match(/Context fetched at:\s*(.+)/);
   180|
   181|  const sha = shaMatch?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
   182|  const fullSha = fullShaMatch?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
   183|  const status = statusMatch?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
   184|  const bootTime = bootMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? 'unknown';
   185|  const env = envMatch?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
   186|  const scheduler = schedulerMatch?.[1] ?? 'unknown';
   187|  const fetchedAt = timestampMatch?.[1]?.trim() ?? new Date().toISOString();
   188|
   189|  const markerLines: string[] = [];
   190|  const markerSection = liveContextBlock.match(/Deploy Markers.*?\n([\s\S]*?)(?:\n\s*Context fetched|\n\[\/IVX)/);
   191|  if (markerSection) {
   192|    const markerMatches = markerSection[1].matchAll(/^\s*(\S+):\s*(.+)$/gm);
   193|    for (const m of markerMatches) {
   194|      markerLines.push(`${m[1]}=${m[2].trim()}`);
   195|    }
   196|  }
   197|
   198|  const markers = markerLines.length > 0 ? ` | Markers: ${markerLines.join(', ')}` : '';
   199|
   200|  return `[LIVE PRODUCTION DATA — USE THIS TO ANSWER PRODUCTION QUESTIONS: commitSHA=${sha} fullSHA=${fullSha} status=${status} bootTime=${bootTime} env=${env} schedulerRunning=${scheduler}${markers} | fetchedAt=${fetchedAt}]`;
   201|}

## IVX IA / Autonomous Audit — current result

**No — IVX IA is not yet at Rork-level autonomous engineering capability.** It has a solid bounded execution foundation, but it cannot honestly be presented as 12 independent engineering developers or a fully autonomous senior-developer platform yet.

### Verified working today
- Production is healthy on commit `362e7f5e…`; GitHub, Render, and provider credentials are configured.
- Durable queue, proof ledger, emergency stop, stage tracking, rollback gates, and two-hour engineering reports exist.
- The narrative brain is evidence-first, bilingual, uses live production context, and avoids unsupported “same as Rork” claims.
- The Android emulator workflow correctly builds a release APK, installs it, launches it, captures logs/screenshots, and runs Maestro QA.

### Critical gaps to close
1. **12 roles are not 12 independent runtimes.** They are shared-worker roles. The actual worker drain is global, sequential, and single-flight.
2. **No per-agent isolation.** To qualify, each agent needs its own runtime/lease, heartbeat, retry budget, queue partition, job history, and durable evidence.
3. **End-to-end production actions are blocked.** Protected audit, run-summary, worker-status, and job-enqueue routes all reject the configured owner tokens as an expired/invalid Supabase session.
4. **Android release QA remains unverified after the signing repair.** The local keystore now reads successfully, but the full release build and GitHub Emulator QA must pass again before any production deployment.
5. **Provider state needs an active inference check.** Credentials report valid, but the live health response currently shows `PROVIDER_VALIDATING`, not a completed ready state.
6. **The certification document is stale.** It states “100% complete” while current runtime evidence still shows the above blockers. That must be corrected so IVX reports reality, not historical claims.

### Upgrade sequence
- Restore owner authentication, then execute the Android-signing repair job with deployment disabled.
- Pass release build + emulator/Maestro QA and retain the artifacts.
- Replace the shared execution loop with isolated runtime workers, each with durable leases and independent evidence.
- Add a real capability scorecard: no agent gets “verified” without a completed task, tests, commit, deploy record, and health proof.
- Run an active provider inference probe and record latency/error evidence.
- Only deploy after all gates pass; then confirm SHA parity, health, and the final proof ledger.

**Current deployment decision: not authorized.** I will not label this live-verified or deploy a new change until the owner session is valid and Android release/emulator QA passes.
